name: F-15C/D Eagle
summary: Twin-engine, twin-tail air-superiority fighter now flown only by a few Air National Guard units as it is replaced by the F-15EX and F-35A.

wings: Large high-mounted wing with about 45 degrees of leading-edge sweep
Cropped (clipped) wingtips and no leading-edge root extensions
Wing area noticeably large for the airframe
engines: Two engines with round nozzles side by side
Big rectangular box intakes on each side of the cockpit, which tilt with the nose
fuselage: Bubble canopy set high on a flat-topped fuselage
Smooth fuselage sides with no conformal fuel tanks
Usually light two-tone air-superiority grey; the D model has a second seat under a longer canopy
tail: Twin vertical fins standing nearly upright, not canted
Horizontal stabilizers with a notched (dogtooth) leading edge

tellTales: Twin upright fins over two round exhausts
Large boxy intakes on the fuselage sides
Smooth-sided single-seat airframe in light grey with no conformal tanks

confusedWith.howToTell: The C model is usually a single-seater in light grey with smooth sides; the Strike Eagle has two seats, conformal tanks along the intakes and often bombs on stub pylons.
The F-15C has upright fins, boxy intakes and round nozzles; the F-22 has outward-canted fins, angular stealth shaping and flat nozzles.
The F-15C is larger with upright fins at the very tail and box intakes; the Hornet has canted fins mounted forward and small intakes under LERX.

usCount.source: USAF FY2026 budget documents / Air National Guard (Fresno, New Orleans, Klamath Falls)
